target.detail: the cashpoint with the extra bit on it

setup: Shimmer in the card slot, pinhole camera up top angled at the keypad, a day's worth of a busy machine's punters writing themselves down.
on_success: Pull the kit at the quiet hour, clone the cards, and spend from three towns over before the first statement lands.
on_fail: The machine got serviced early and the engineer knows exactly what your little extra is and where the camera points — at you.
on_crit: A business account went through with a fat float on it. One card, a very good week.

target.name: the runners
target.detail: the cloned cards and a shopping list

setup: Stack of cloned cards, a list of what buys clean and resells fast — gift cards, spirits, the odd laptop — and a couple of youngers to walk them in.
on_success: Spread across a dozen tills so no one card gets warm. Convert to clean goods, goods to cash, cash to gone.
on_fail: One runner gets greedy at the till, tries it twice, the card declines loud and the security guard was bored anyway.
on_crit: A card with no limit anyone's found yet. You stop before you get greedy. Just.

target.detail: the outer pump the CCTV can't quite reach

setup: Pay-at-pump station, one bank of pumps angled away from the kiosk camera. A cloned card in your pocket and a full tank's worth of nerve. Nobody watches pump six.
on_success: Card in, pump runs, receipt declined into your pocket. You fill two jerry cans in the boot as well, because a tank's a tank.
on_fail: The pump asks for a postcode you don't have and holds the transaction while it thinks about you on camera.

target.name: Denise
target.detail: a stack of cards good for one tap each before they trip

setup: Cloned cards, none of them worth a proper spend, all of them good for a contactless tap under the limit. A high street full of tills that don't ask twice.
on_success: You tap your way down the parade — coffee, phone case, two meal deals, a bottle of something — and bin each card before it can say no.
on_fail: Third shop, the card beeps the wrong colour and the girl behind the till already has her finger on the button under the counter.
on_crit: One of the cards isn't clipped at all. It just keeps working, tap after tap, all the way to the retail park.

target.detail: a business card with a fat float sitting on it

setup: Hotel check-in with a cloned corporate card, the kind with a spending limit that could buy a car. The receptionist's more worried about your bags than your details.
on_success: Room booked, minibar emptied, spa treatments billed to a company that won't notice for a month. You check out before the pre-auth clears into a charge.
on_fail: The card flags on the pre-authorisation and the duty manager appears with the specific calm of someone trained for exactly this.

target.detail: a delivery address that isn't yours and never was

setup: An empty flat with a working letterbox, a laptop, and a list of card numbers. Order the small dear things — phones, gift cards, perfume — and let the couriers do the crime for you.
on_success: Parcels stack up on the mat of a flat that belongs to nobody. You collect once, convert twice, and the address never sees you.
on_fail: The card company's fraud team flags the address before the courier does, and there's a very still car outside when you go to collect.

target.detail: the hole in the wall outside the shut-up bank

setup: A shimmer thin as a bus ticket already sitting in the card slot, a pinhole camera on the light fitting above the keypad, and a whole day's worth of a busy machine writing itself down for you.
on_success: You pull the kit at the dead hour, clone the night's takings, and spend them three towns over before the first statement lands on a doormat.
on_fail: An engineer's out early servicing the machine and he knows exactly what your little extra is, and exactly where the pinhole's pointing.
on_crit: A business account went through the machine with the weekend's float still on it. One card, a very good week.

target.detail: the cab firm that lets the driver key the amount

setup: Minicab with a card reader the driver types the fare into himself. Cloned card, a long fake journey, and a cut for a driver who's decided he doesn't earn enough to have a conscience.
on_success: A forty-mile fare that never happened, split down the middle at the rank, and a receipt for a trip to an airport you never saw.
on_fail: The driver bottles it halfway and cancels the transaction, and now two people know and only one of them is calm.

target.detail: a card machine glued into a fake collection tin

setup: A tabard, a lanyard, and a tap-to-donate tin rigged to a reader that isn't a charity's. The precinct on a Saturday is full of people who'd rather tap than make eye contact.
on_success: A pound a tap, a hundred taps an hour, and everyone walks away feeling good about themselves. Nobody checks where good feelings go.
on_fail: A woman who actually volunteers for the real charity clocks a logo that's a shade wrong and won't stop asking questions.

target.name: Yusuf
target.detail: first-years who'll walk cards in for a cut of nothing

setup: Cloned cards and a couple of skint students who'll do the walking for beer money. A retail park, a shopping list of things that resell in a day, and youngers who don't know how deep this goes.
on_success: They buy, you convert, everyone eats. The kids think it's a laugh. You let them, because the day they understand is the day they want more.
on_fail: One of them gets greedy at the till, tries the card twice, and the security guard was already bored enough to care.
